data.stem: In which Part and Articles of the Constitution are the Fundamental Rights listed?
data.explanation: Part III covering Articles 12 to 35 is correct because the text groups the justiciable Fundamental Rights there. Part IV covering Directive Principles is wrong because it guides the State but is not directly enforceable, while Parts V and VI concern the Union and the States and do not list Fundamental Rights.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Right under Part III today?
data.explanation: Right to Property is correct as the NOT answer because the 44th Amendment in 1978 moved it to Article 300A. Equality covering Articles 14 to 18, religion covering Articles 25 to 28, and protection against exploitation covering Articles 23 and 24 are wrong as NOT answers because they remain Fundamental Rights.
data.label: practice

data.stem: The Right to Property is now protected as a constitutional right under which Article?
data.explanation: Article 300A is correct because it says no person shall be deprived of property save by authority of law. Article 19 is wrong because it lists citizen freedoms only, Article 21A is wrong because it covers education, and Article 32 is wrong because it provides the remedy.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Article 19 freedoms are guaranteed to whom?
options: All citizens and foreigners resident in India
All persons with domicile in India
data.explanation: Citizens only is correct because Article 19 is expressly limited to citizens. All persons is wrong because that wider scope belongs to Article 21, while the other options wrongly add foreigners and domicile as qualifying groups.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Free and compulsory education for children aged six to fourteen years is guaranteed by which provision?
data.explanation: Article 21A is correct because it is the Fundamental Right inserted in 2002 for ages six to fourteen. Article 45 is wrong because it is a Directive Principle on early childhood care, Article 46 is wrong because it concerns weaker sections, and Article 30 is wrong because it concerns minority institutions.
data.label: practice

data.stem: How many freedoms does Article 19 list?
data.explanation: Six freedoms is correct counting speech, assembly, association, movement, residence and profession. Four freedoms is wrong because it undercounts by two, five freedoms is wrong because it undercounts by one, and seven freedoms is wrong because it reflects the pre-1978 count before deletions.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which Article protects life and personal liberty except by procedure established by law?
data.explanation: Article 21 is correct because it is the life and personal liberty guarantee. Article 19 is wrong because it lists citizen freedoms, Article 20 is wrong because it safeguards conviction, and Article 22 is wrong because it safeguards arrest and detention.
data.label: practice

data.stem: A High Court issues writs for enforcement of Fundamental Rights and also for which other rights?
data.explanation: Other legal rights as well is correct because Article 226 reaches beyond Part III. Only Fundamental Rights is wrong because it confuses Article 226 with Article 32, while only Directive Principles and only service matters are wrong because they narrow the High Court power incorrectly.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which writ commands a public authority to perform a public duty?
data.explanation: Mandamus is correct because it directs performance of a public duty. Prohibition is wrong because it restrains a lower court from acting beyond jurisdiction, certiorari is wrong because it quashes proceedings, and quo warranto is wrong because it questions a claim to public office.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Article 32 guarantees the right to move which court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights?
data.explanation: Supreme Court is correct because Article 32 confers the guaranteed remedy there. High Court is wrong because it acts under Article 226, while District Court and Tribunal are wrong because they lack Part III writ jurisdiction.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which Directive Principle provisions are associated in the OPSC item with overriding Article 14 for economic redistribution?
data.explanation: Article 39(b) and (c) is correct because the OPSC 2025 item pairs resource ownership and concentration concerns with the equality question. Article 14 and 15 are wrong because they are the equality provisions themselves, while Article 18 and Article 19 clauses are wrong because they concern titles and freedoms.
data.label: pyq-pattern

data.stem: During a national emergency, enforcement of which articles cannot be suspended after the 44th Amendment?
data.explanation: Articles 20 and 21 is correct because the 44th Amendment protects their enforcement. Articles 14 and 19 are wrong because their enforcement can be suspended, while Articles 32 and 226 as remedies are wrong because Articles 20 and 21 are the protected rights themselves.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which amendment inserted Article 21A on education for ages six to fourteen?
data.explanation: 86th Amendment Act, 2002 is correct because it inserted Article 21A effective 1 April 2010. The 44th Amendment is wrong because it removed property, the 42nd Amendment is wrong because it concerned Fundamental Duties and other changes, and the 73rd Amendment is wrong because it concerned Panchayati Raj.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Articles 23 and 24 prohibit what?
options: Traffic in human beings, forced labour and hazardous child employment
data.explanation: Traffic, forced labour and hazardous child employment is correct under Articles 23 and 24. Religious instruction is wrong because it belongs to Articles 25 to 28, untouchability and titles are wrong because they belong to Article 17 and 18, and detention safeguards are wrong because they belong to Article 22.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which writ secures release from unlawful detention?
data.explanation: Habeas corpus is correct because it directs production and release from unlawful detention. Mandamus is wrong because it commands a duty, prohibition is wrong because it restrains a court, and certiorari is wrong because it quashes proceedings.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Consider the following statements: 1. Fundamental Rights are justiciable. 2. Directive Principles are directly enforceable through Article 32. Which is correct?
data.explanation: 1 only is correct because Part III rights are justiciable while Directive Principles are not enforceable through Article 32. The option with 2 only and both are wrong because they treat Directive Principles as directly enforceable, while neither is wrong because the first statement is correct.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which writ is issued to question a person's claim to a public office?
data.explanation: Quo warranto is correct because it asks by what authority a person holds public office. Mandamus is wrong because it commands a duty, certiorari is wrong because it quashes proceedings, and prohibition is wrong because it restrains a court from continuing.
data.label: practice

data.stem: A state law imposes reasonable restrictions on speech on grounds of public order. Under which article is this provided?
data.explanation: Article 19(2) is correct because it lists the restriction grounds for speech and expression. Article 14 is wrong because it concerns equality, Article 21 is wrong because it concerns life and liberty, and Article 300A is wrong because it concerns property.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Article 32 from Article 226?
options: Article 32 is High Court power and Article 226 is Supreme Court power
Article 32 covers Fundamental Rights only, while Article 226 also covers other legal rights
data.explanation: Article 32 covering Fundamental Rights only while Article 226 also covers other legal rights is correct. Both identical is wrong because their scopes differ, the reversed courts option is wrong because it swaps the two articles, and only Directive Principles is wrong because it understates Article 226.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which single statement about cultural and educational rights is correct?
options: Article 30 allows minorities to establish and administer educational institutions
Cultural rights are in Part IV and non-justiciable
Article 30 is suspended during emergencies without exception
data.explanation: Article 30 allowing minorities to establish institutions is correct under Part III. Article 29 protecting only individuals is wrong because it protects sections of citizens and language, culture and script, while Part IV location and automatic suspension claims are wrong because these rights are justiciable Part III rights.
data.label: practice

data.stem:
Consider the following statements regarding the protections in Article 20:
1. The bar on retrospective laws applies to criminal punishment but not to taxes.
2. Protection against being punished twice also covers departmental inquiries.
3. Taking a blood sample from an accused does not breach the guarantee against self-incrimination.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
data.explanation: 1 and 3 only is correct: ex-post-facto protection reaches criminal law alone, so a tax may be retrospective, and physical evidence such as blood samples is outside self-incrimination. Statement 2 is wrong because double jeopardy applies only before courts and judicial tribunals, so options including it are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: The view that Article 21 guards only against executive action, and not against an unfair law, was overturned in which judgement?
data.explanation: Maneka Gandhi (1978) is correct: it overruled Gopalan (1950) and required any procedure to be fair, just and reasonable. Kesavananda concerned the amending power, Indra Sawhney dealt with OBC reservation and Unni Krishnan with free education, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: A person is being held in a private house against his will. Which writ can a court issue directly against the private individual holding him?
data.explanation: Habeas corpus is correct because it lies against public authorities and private persons alike and orders the detainee to be produced. Mandamus is wrong as it runs only against public bodies, whereas prohibition and certiorari are addressed to lower courts or tribunals, so they are incorrect here.
data.label: practice

data.stem:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 31B and the Ninth Schedule were added by the First Amendment Act, 1951.
2. Laws placed in the Ninth Schedule after 24 April 1973 can be challenged for damaging the basic structure.
3. The Supreme Court upheld, in Minerva Mills, the 42nd Amendment's extension of Article 31C to all Directive Principles.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
data.explanation: 1 and 2 only is correct: the First Amendment created Article 31B with the Schedule, and Waman Rao and Coelho opened post-1973 entries to basic-structure review. Statement 3 is wrong because Minerva Mills struck down that 42nd Amendment extension, so options including 3 are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: A foreign national, not an enemy alien, lives in India. Which of these rights can she claim?
options: Protection of life and personal liberty (Article 21)
Freedom to reside and settle anywhere in India (Article 19)
Right to conserve a distinct culture (Article 29)
data.explanation: Article 21 is correct because it protects every person, citizen or not. Articles 16, 19 and 29 are wrong answers: along with Articles 15 and 30 they are expressly reserved for citizens, so a foreigner cannot invoke them.
data.label: practice
